headline: Jio allotment day as markets brace for a Fed week with Brent near 115 dollars

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Monday, the twenty-sixth of October, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most this morning. First, a week of central banks. The US Federal Reserve meets on Tuesday and Wednesday, the European Central Bank decides on Thursday and the Bank of Japan on Friday. With Brent crude still around 115 dollars a barrel and the US ten-year yield near 5 percent, markets are now betting on a Fed rate hike by December.

Second, it's allotment day for the Jio Platforms IPO. The record offer was booked more than 22 times, and the shares are due to list on Wednesday, the same day the Fed announces its decision.

And third, Indian stocks start the week bruised. The Nifty fell for four sessions in a row last week, and Economic Times says Indian valuations are now at a six-year low. GIFT Nifty points to a flat to slightly lower start.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Let's look back at last week. In a holiday-shortened week of four sessions, the Sensex fell 1,605 points, or 2.15 percent, and the Nifty lost 546 points, or 2.36 percent, to close at about 22,600. On Friday alone the Nifty slipped about 0.4 percent. Mint notes the Nifty is now down about 13.6 percent so far this year.

The broader market took the heavier blow. Moneycontrol says mid-caps had their steepest weekly fall in two years, with Swiggy, KEI Industries and Motilal Oswal Financial among the biggest drags. The total value of BSE-listed companies fell by about 20.8 lakh crore rupees in four sessions. Bank Nifty lost nearly 2.8 percent and slipped below 55,000. HDFC Bank alone shed about 55,500 crore rupees of market value, and Bajaj Finance about 34,200 crore. IT was the only sector to gain, and Tata Consultancy Services and Larsen and Toubro were the only two of the ten biggest companies to add value.

On flows, foreign institutional investors were net buyers on Friday, of 887 crore rupees, and domestic institutions bought 3,236 crore rupees, their fourth straight day of buying. But for October so far, foreign investors have pulled out about 48,056 crore rupees from Indian shares.

The levels analysts are watching: Friday's low near 22,372 as immediate support, then about 22,180. Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities says a decisive break below 22,180 could open the way to 22,000 or even 21,850. On the upside, 22,800 to 22,850 is seen as resistance.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
The primary market stays busy. Five mainboard issues open this week, together seeking close to 2,600 crore rupees. They are EAAA India Alternatives, SFC Environmental Technologies, M K Sons Fine Jewels, BLS Polymers and Bombay Coated and Special Steels. SFC Environmental, a wastewater treatment company, opens on Tuesday, the twenty-seventh, and closes on Thursday. Ahead of it, Abakkus, Carnelian and IIFL were among five investors who picked up a 3 percent stake.

Three companies list this week, led by Jio Platforms.

Now to deals. Senco Gold has agreed to buy a 68 percent stake in August Jewellery, which runs the Melorra brand, for 68 crore rupees, in tranches to be completed by February next year. KEC International won transmission orders worth 2,872 crore rupees, including from Power Grid. And VRL Logistics' share buyback opens tomorrow, the twenty-seventh, and closes on the second of November.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
First, the big picture on earnings. An Economic Times tally of the September quarter so far shows revenue up 22.1 percent and net profit up 27.5 percent. But banks, IT and pharma are lagging the rest.

In banking, Kotak Mahindra Bank's net profit rose 26 percent to 5,645 crore rupees, according to Moneycontrol. IDFC First Bank's profit nearly tripled to 1,045 crore rupees, on net interest income up 21 percent, although its net interest margin narrowed to 5.6 percent.

In IT, the debate is still about Infosys. Its deal wins were strong at 5.2 billion dollars, but it trimmed its full-year growth outlook. Mint says that leaves it trailing key rivals, and Moneycontrol's research team says weak guidance overshadowed the bookings, pointing to productivity gains from AI and pricing pressure.

In pharma, Dr Reddy's grew its India business, but sales of its cancer drug Revlimid fell in North America. The company is pinning hopes on a relaunch of generic semaglutide and the US launch of an abatacept biosimilar.

Today's results include Tata Consumer, Paytm, ITC Hotels and APL Apollo Tubes. Later this week, REC, Coal India, NTPC, BEL and Godrej Consumer are due.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the bond market, where the pressure is building. The ten-year government bond yield rose to about 7.47 percent on the twenty-third, from about 7.19 percent on the sixth of October, a jump of nearly 30 basis points since the Reserve Bank's policy review. Experts cite oil, global yields, tighter liquidity and expectations of more rate hikes. V Ramachandra Reddy of Karur Vysya Bank warns that if yields stay high, the cost of funding the fiscal deficit will rise.

On the external side, India's crude import bill jumped 46 percent to 90.6 billion dollars in April to September, and the Indian crude basket has averaged about 121 dollars a barrel this month. Forex reserves fell about 5 billion dollars to 721 billion dollars in the week to the sixteenth.

For the corporate world, two items. The corporate affairs ministry has extended the deadline for filing annual financial statements for last financial year to the thirty-first of December, and annual returns to the thirty-first of January, with no additional fee. That follows problems on the MCA 21 portal. And large companies are preparing for Ind AS 118, which brings new ways of classifying income and expenses and reporting operating profit. Audit committees are discussing transition plans while they wait for final rules.

The market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, plans to review its short-selling and securities lending rules, ease norms for buybacks and offers for sale, and add safeguards against misuse of trading terminals, according to chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey.

On trade, negotiations on the India and European Union free trade agreement have concluded, and the Rotterdam port chief says the hope is to sign it by year-end.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Oil eased a little this morning. Brent was down about 1.3 percent at around 115 dollars a barrel, and US crude about 1.6 percent lower at nearly 102 dollars, as diplomatic efforts continue. But Brent had crossed 117 dollars last week, and Ajit Mishra of Religare Broking says the near-term bias remains bullish but highly driven by headlines from West Asia and the Strait of Hormuz.

On Wall Street, the Dow fell 1.23 percent on Friday, the S&P 500 lost about half a percent and the Nasdaq 0.2 percent. US consumer sentiment hit one of its lowest readings in the survey's 74-year history. This week, Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon report results, which will test the optimism around spending on AI.

Gold has slipped below 4,000 dollars an ounce. Analysts quoted by Business Standard expect gold and silver to stay under pressure until the Fed gives clearer signals.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script: An update on the Jio IPO you're following. Allotment is due today through the registrar KFin Technologies. Over the weekend, Mint reported a grey market premium of about 250 rupees a share, which it says points to a possible listing near 1,369 rupees, about 22 percent above the top of the band. Listing is planned for Wednesday at 10 in the morning.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
First, a note for anyone heading to a branch today. Banks in several cities, including Bengaluru, Chandigarh, Shimla, Srinagar, Jammu and Agartala, are closed for regional holidays, though online banking works as usual.

If you applied for the Jio IPO and get no shares, the blocked money in your account will be released. One lot of 12 shares costs 13,428 rupees at the top price.

On deposits, Indian Bank has raised rates by 15 basis points on its 555-day and 777-day special fixed deposits, from the twenty-third of October. With yields rising, Mint reports fund managers are divided on gilt funds. Higher yields offer a chance to lock in, but inflation, crude and further rate hikes could push yields higher still.

For property sellers, a tax reminder. Long-term capital gains on land or buildings can be exempted by investing in Section 54EC bonds, up to 50 lakh rupees, within six months of the sale, with a five-year lock-in.

On insurance, the regulator, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India, has extended the deadline for feedback on its commission proposals to the thirty-first of October. Non-bank lenders are asking for a five-year transition, saying the proposed caps of 2 percent on credit life cover and 5 percent on credit health cover would make selling these policies unviable.

And an investor warning. The market regulator is urging investors to check three things before acting on a viral tip: that the adviser is registered, that the trading app is genuine, and where the payment is going.

That's the brief for today. What to watch: how the Nifty holds the 22,372 and 22,180 levels after four losing days, today's results from Tata Consumer and Paytm, your Jio allotment status, and crude oil ahead of the Fed's decision on Wednesday. Have a good Monday.
